question: Does independently reconstructing requested rows remove stream block-decode amplification while retaining useful COMPLETE-branch savings?
sources: All six existing fully trained Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-4B full-key sources, seeds 3/7/11. No new fitting, padding, replicated keys or random vector benchmarks.

row-xor: fixed original first-row anchor with independent masks

controls: Direct original standalone FAISS codes and all declared byte codecs with identical blocks/compiler/library/request adapter. Original code bytes, codebooks and original-ID decoded vectors must hash identically.
requests: 32 real calibration and 32 official test token prefixes per source, identical to the previous CPU lane; preserve original token addressing and original trained row IDs.
timing: Six concurrent lanes on disjoint fixed physical cores, one thread each. New handles with first-request timings; two warmups and five request sweeps, warm OS with zero application cache. Full token-addressing/adapter and row-only timings reported separately. No GPU timing claim in this addendum.
selection: Independently within each unchanged decoded FAISS codec and byte-compressor family, lowest calibration complete-token p50 among candidates saving at least 1% or 10% of COMPLETE branch bytes versus direct. If none qualify, use direct fallback. Test timings never choose or change layout. All 1044 cells retained (6 sources x 6 codecs x (1 direct + 4 layouts x 7 compressors/predictors)).
metrics: complete branch bytes including maps/codebooks/common model
claim_boundary: This is a generic lossless byte-access layout composed over unchanged FAISS codes. It is distinct from the DATrie prefix/suffix mark-compact contribution and cannot be called universally faster or smaller. Fixed anchors may fail to compress high-entropy rows; raw fallback and losing layouts remain evidence. These six trained branches do not establish billion-row capacity or full Engram pretraining.
publication: Large bundles, requests, trained rows and corpora remain task artifacts; only compact evidence and code enter Git.
